role.altitude: The nanosystems engineer keeps designing materials and processes, judging safety, reviewing supplier work and running pilots; looking up substance data one by one, compiling consumption logs, chasing supplier status by mail and rebuilding balance sheets shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using substance databases and saved queries
role.ambitious_version: An engineer who compares more design options because the data behind each one assemble themselves.

tasks.short: Set requirements, check substance rules and toxicity data, design nano-enabled products with reduced toxicity, increased durability or improved energy efficiency, estimate lifecycle effects, and review the design.

steps.what: Engineer sets product requirements including toxicity and durability targets
Engineer checks substance rules and toxicity data for candidate nanomaterials
Engineer designs the nano-enabled products' composition and structure
Engineer estimates lifecycle effects: energy use and durability
Engineer reviews the design with the team

tasks.design: A saved query on a substance database returns registration status and hazard data for the list of candidate nanomaterials, instead of the engineer looking up each one. A parameterised lifecycle model estimates energy use and lifetime for a design variant from a few inputs. Setting requirements, designing and reviewing stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Substance data were looked up one by one and lifecycle sheets rebuilt per variant.
tasks.enabler_now: Substance databases with saved queries and parameterised lifecycle models.
tasks.still_hard: New nanoforms with little hazard data.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a safer material that still performs.

reach.learn: Whether hazards are flagged earlier in design.

evidence.claim: Substance databases list registration status and hazard data per substance.

assumptions: Boundary: designing nano-enabled products; testing new products (task 16542) and CAD design (task 16544) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: candidate substances listed in the substance database, about 60% of them for new nanoforms; s2 is priced at that share.
Setting requirements, designing and reviewing keep their full time.
unknowns: Coverage of nanoforms in the substance database.
research_questions: Are safer alternatives chosen more often?

incremental.description: Engineer keeps the lifecycle model inputs current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: novel nanoforms; high: known material families.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Send specifications to suppliers, track supplier progress, review supplier designs and test results, meet suppliers to resolve issues, and record decisions to coordinate or supervise the work of suppliers or vendors on nanosystem devices.

steps.what: Engineer sends specifications and requirements to suppliers or vendors
Engineer tracks supplier progress and deliverables in a spreadsheet from their mails
Supplier updates milestone status in the supplier portal
Engineer reviews supplier designs and test results for lenses, probes or other devices
Engineer meets suppliers and resolves issues
Engineer records decisions and actions and mails them to the supplier

tasks.design: A supplier portal holds the milestones and deliverables per supplier. Suppliers update their own status and upload test results, so the engineer reads one view instead of compiling a spreadsheet from mails. Decisions and actions are logged in the same portal and both sides see them, instead of minutes being typed and mailed. Sending specifications, reviewing supplier work and resolving issues stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier status arrived by mail and was compiled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Supplier portals with milestones and shared action logs.
tasks.still_hard: Small suppliers who will not use a portal.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a supplier to put the best people on a hard part.

evidence.claim: Mail and attachments glue supplier work today; shared portals replace them.

assumptions: Boundary: coordinating suppliers; supervising own technicians (task 16532) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s2: about 60% of suppliers update the portal; s2 is priced at that share.
s2 saves compiling mails into a status sheet; s6 saves typing and mailing minutes.
Suppliers' update time is shown in s3 and is about what their status mails took.
unknowns: Number of active suppliers per project.

incremental.description: Engineer keeps milestones in the portal current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few suppliers on the portal; high: most suppliers on the portal.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Map current water, chemical and energy use and waste, design nano-based manufacturing processes that use less, calculate resource balances, run pilot trials, and compare results.

steps.what: Engineer maps current water, chemical and energy use and waste production
Engineer designs nano-based manufacturing process changes
Engineer calculates water, chemical and energy balances for the options
Engineer runs pilot trials of the new process
Engineer compares pilot results and selects the process

tasks.design: Water, chemical and energy use per process step come from meters and the production system on a dashboard, instead of being compiled from logs. A parameterised mass and energy balance model computes the balance for each process option from a few inputs, instead of a new spreadsheet each time. Designing the process, running pilots and choosing stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Consumption was compiled from logs and balances rebuilt for each option.
tasks.enabler_now: Production dashboards and parameterised balance models.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which rinse step can be dropped without losing yield.

evidence.claim: Recurring status reports become a dashboard; calculations are deterministic.

assumptions: Boundary: designing resource-saving processes; engineering production processes (task 16541) and pilot production equipment (task 16539) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: about 60% of process steps are metered; s1 is priced at that share.
Designing, piloting and choosing keep their full time.
research_questions: Are more options compared before piloting?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few meters; high: metered lines and repeat options.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review site contamination data, review evidence on nanocatalysts and nanofiltration for the pollutants, design the nanosystems to clean specific pollutants from hazardous waste sites, check release risks, and plan field tests.

steps.what: Engineer reviews contamination data for the hazardous waste site
Engineer reviews evidence on nanocatalysts and nanofiltration for the pollutants

loop.input: The pollutants and a literature database.
loop.output: Ranked papers with short summaries, each linked to its source.
loop.check: The engineer opens every cited paper before use.
loop.stop: The engineer searches by hand when known key papers are missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Results are spread over chemistry and engineering venues.

steps.what: Engineer designs the nanosystems to clean the specific pollutants
Engineer checks release and safety risks of the nanomaterials on site
Engineer plans the field test with the site owner and authority

tasks.design: Site investigation results come from the project data store as tables per sample point and pollutant, instead of being picked from report PDFs. A literature search returns ranked papers with linked summaries, and the engineer opens every source. Designing the nanosystem, checking release risks and planning the field test stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site data sat in report PDFs and literature was searched by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Project data stores and literature search with citations.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether nanoparticles could spread beyond the site.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; design and safety judgement stay.

reach.learn: Whether test plans address release risks.

evidence.claim: Literature work suits an answer desk with citations.

assumptions: Boundary: designing remediation nanosystems; nanoparticle catalysts for pollutants (task 19672) and research on nanotechnology topics (task 16546) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: investigation results stored as data tables by the site investigator, for about 60% of sites; s1 is priced at that share.
Designing, risk checks and planning keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of sites with data tables.

incremental.description: Engineer opens and checks cited papers.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: sites with report PDFs only; high: sites with data tables.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
